episode_title: Why Culture Beats Demographics with Matt Lawler

real_qa.q: How did Matt Lawler transition from philosophy and economics into data and insights strategy?
real_qa.r: Lawler started as a philosophy and economics major planning to attend law school and MBA, but in 2003 during a small recession, he took a part-time data entry role at Warner Brothers managing rights and clearances for the International TV Group. Finding the work engaging but only requiring 3-4 hours daily, he spent time with the marketing team on the second floor, eventually taking an analytics role tied to marketing. He went back to business school, then returned to Warner Brothers in audience development, leveraging social media to drive TV consumption, which launched his career in understanding consumer behavior across multiple platforms.
real_qa.requete: Matt Lawler career path philosophy economics data

real_qa.q: What measurable impact did the Crypto.com Arena naming rights deal show on brand perception?
real_qa.r: Over a five-year longitudinal study, AEG found that 20 to 30 percent growth occurred in how both local and national sports fans perceive crypto.com as a trustworthy brand with a good reputation and as a stable company. This was particularly important given crypto's reputation challenges, and the partnership helped solidify crypto.com's credibility with fans as the company consistently stayed the course.
real_qa.requete: Crypto.com Arena naming rights brand perception study results

real_qa.q: Why does AEG consider Los Angeles the best live event market globally?
real_qa.r: Los Angeles hosts major sporting events including the World Cup, Super Bowl, and Olympics within a three-year period, and the city's unique geography and climate diversity create natural competition with alternative entertainment like Disneyland, beaches, hiking at Runyon Canyon, and snowboarding at Bear Mountain. Additionally, LA is the most saturated professional sports market in North America with ten teams, and many AEG fans globally support teams like Galaxy and Kings, allowing the company to attract national and international brand partnerships beyond just the local market.
real_qa.requete: Los Angeles best live event market sports entertainment

real_qa.q: What role did the Obama 2008 presidential campaign play in Lawler's understanding of social media's business value?
real_qa.r: Lawler was enthralled by how Obama's campaign used social media in a way no presidential candidate had before, meticulously using media to drive excitement around hope and the idea of being the first Black president. He spent considerable time learning from these mediums, and it reinforced his belief that there was real weight to social media, especially when his employer Warner Brothers recognized the need to figure out how social media worked for their business.
real_qa.requete: Obama 2008 campaign social media marketing influence

real_qa.q: How do live events create relationship building advantages over digital and online experiences?
real_qa.r: Over the past five years, companies invested heavily in moving online through Zoom, Teams, remote work, and virtual shows, but live events create relationship building that is unmatched because humans have millennia of being in physical proximity in their DNA and nature. Even major streaming platforms and content creators like MrBeast build event strategies because sticky engagement happens in-person, and in-person tangible value multiplies all other marketing work and solidifies relationships in ways digital channels cannot replicate.
real_qa.requete: live events better than digital engagement relationship building

real_qa.q: What was the scale of the Crypto.com Arena naming rights deal for AEG?
real_qa.r: Lawler stated there are 700 plus million reasons why AEG made the Crypto.com Arena naming rights deal, describing it as really important for the company, and highlighting that naming rights deals represent significant brand partnership value that many people do not realize.
real_qa.requete: Crypto.com Arena naming deal value AEG partnership

guest.bio_context: Matt Lawler began his career at Warner Brothers in 2003 in the legal department managing rights and clearances for the International TV Group, then transitioned to the marketing team where he developed analytics capabilities. He attended business school and worked in audience development at Warner Brothers, harnessing social media to drive TV consumption, before building social media buying teams at an agency. He joined AEG to lead digital strategy leveraging technology and first-party ticketing data to drive brand partnerships across sports, music, and live events.
